problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a collection of freight parcels into standardized shipping pallets. The parcels are labeled as follows:

* Parcel Alpha: mass 41kg
* Parcel Bravo: mass 58kg
* Parcel Charlie: mass 44kg
* Parcel Delta: mass 32kg
* Parcel Echo: mass 35kg
* Parcel Foxtrot: mass 44kg
* Parcel Golf: mass 55kg
* Parcel Hotel: mass 55kg
* Parcel India: mass 57kg
* Parcel Juliett: mass 70kg
* Parcel Kilo: mass 31kg
* Parcel Lima: mass 39kg
* Parcel Mike: mass 69kg
* Parcel November: mass 48kg
* Parcel Oscar: mass 49kg
* Parcel Papa: mass 32kg
* Parcel Quebec: mass 66kg
* Parcel Romeo: mass 43kg
* Parcel Sierra: mass 49kg
* Parcel Tango: mass 61kg
* Parcel Uniform: mass 54kg
* Parcel Victor: mass 37kg
* Parcel Whiskey: mass 69kg
* Parcel X-ray: mass 52kg
* Parcel Yankee: mass 35kg
* Parcel Zulu: mass 59kg
* Parcel Asterisk: mass 53kg
* Parcel Backslash: mass 44kg
* Parcel Bracket: mass 69kg
* Parcel Caret: mass 67kg
* Parcel Underscore: mass 32kg
* Parcel Grave: mass 36kg
* Parcel a: mass 52kg
* Parcel b: mass 59kg
* Parcel c: mass 42kg

Every pallet possesses a maximum safe load capacity of 100 kilograms. The coordinator must ensure every parcel is assigned to precisely one pallet, with the cumulative mass on any given pallet never surpassing its rated limit. The objective is to accomplish this allocation while employing the minimal possible number of pallets.
